title: Temporal retention policy visualizer and automated compliance handoff for prompt/response telemetry
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Customers and auditors struggle to understand how multiple retention rules (per-tenant, per-route, per-model, sampled telemetry) interact over time, and how evidence bundles will be constructed when data spans different regions and TTLs. Goal: Ship a Temporal Retention Visualizer in Console and an automated compliance handoff pipeline that 1) visualizes effective TTLs and sampling across tenants/routes/models and regions, 2) simulates what data will be exported as evidence for a given legal hold or audit window, and 3) generates an attestable evidence bundle with provenance metadata and signed manifests. Scope: prompts, responses, request logs, and aggregated metrics; per-route/tenant overrides and sampled retention; cross-region residency awareness; simulated and real evidence export. Out of scope for MVP: full per-token PII redaction workflows and HSM signing at scale (will be handled by follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Console: Temporal visualizer UI shows timeline for a selected tenant+route with stacked layers for: raw prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics; effective TTL calculation (inheritance and overrides) is shown and can be toggled to show origin policies

Simulator: Given a date range and tenant+route selection, simulator outputs the precise set of records that would be retained vs expired and a sample evidence bundle (JSON manifest + file references) matching retention rules

Export: Automated evidence handoff endpoint produces a signed archive (or mock-signed for MVP) containing: exported records, manifest with retention policies applied, region/residency tags, and audit log of transformations
API contract: engineers receive an RFC with clear JSON schema for the manifest and endpoints for evidence export and TTL resolution
Telemetry: Events emitted for visualizer usage, simulator runs, and export initiation, including performance metrics and error codes
Security: Security team signs off on data-in-transit and at-rest protections for exported bundles and on the security_review_required checklist
engineering_notes: Core requirement: TTL resolution service that accepts tenant, route, model, timestamp and returns effective TTL and source rule (inheritance path). Prefer implementing as a lightweight microservice (stateless cache + persisted policy store).
Sampling: Simulator must be able to apply deterministic sampling to reproduce which records are retained; implement sample seeds tied to tenant+route and time window for auditability.

Evidence manifest schema: flat JSON fields only for MVP - bundle_id, tenant_id, route_id, time_window_start, time_window_end, file_refs[], policy_references[], region_tags[], signature_placeholder. Full schema to be included in RFC.
Storage: exported bundles should be stored in encrypted S3 buckets with customer-scoped prefixes; initial MVP will use a temporary signed URL for download; later work will wire to tenant KMS/HSM.
Performance: Simulator runs should be batched and use time-windowed index scans on logs. Engineering to prototype with 30-day window and benchmark runtime under typical request volumes.
Fallbacks: If cross-region data cannot be instantly included in bundle, system should annotate manifest with missing shards and provide asynchronous completion.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): Console visualizer + simulator + mock-signed evidence export available to internal reviewers and select customers behind feature flag. Phase 2: add real signing with KMS/HSM, automated long-running export jobs, and per-tenant retention policy editor. Communication: early access announcement, runbook for support, and KB article with example manifests.
compliance_impact: Provides clear evidence generation and reproducible retention simulations to support audits and legal holds. Reduces manual effort and risk in proving data residency and retention adherence.
